html:
SMTO-HTTP-0035 — The service's reply was too large for SMTO to accept

GUID: ee71e7cc-05ea-41cf-a70d-c107bf93e529
Slug: http-encoded-response-limit
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service sent more data than this request is allowed to receive, so SMTO stopped reading partway through and didn't use the reply as the answer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run the task again and ask for less at once, for example one page, a shorter date range, or only the fields you need. A narrower request produces a reply that fits within the size limit.
  2. If the service offers page-by-page results or search filters, ask the task to use them. Splitting the data into pages keeps each reply small enough to accept.
  3. If the task was changing something, check on the service whether that change already happened before running it again. The service did answer, so it received the request even though the reply was too large.

What success looks like

  • The narrower request returns a complete answer without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Switching to a Model with a bigger memory won't raise this limit, and don't delete earlier results or saved work to make room.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The encoded response exceeded the request's max_response_bytes plus 65,536 bytes before a complete decoded body was obtained, so the Gateway stopped reading.

What this means

  • Encoded response bytes exceeded max_response_bytes plus 65,536 before a complete supported decoded body was obtained. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Encoded response bytes exceeded max_response_bytes plus 65,536 before a complete supported decoded body was obtained.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare encoded input bound with the chosen decoded response bound; they are separate limits.

How to fix it

  • Narrow the remote query (pagination, filters, field selection) or request a smaller representation so the body fits within max_response_bytes plus 64 KiB of encoded input. Increasing model context does not raise this transfer limit.
  • Reduce the remote query or request a bounded representation. Increasing model context does not raise the transport limit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A narrower provider-supported response fits both encoded and decoded bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
